choices.reason: A lower-loading m125 point at 2/1 separates the strong V2 response seen at 2/1 in 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4 from a possible loading contribution, using the 0/1, 1/1, 2/1, and 5/1 m125 observations as a local response curve.
This lower-loading 5/1 m125 point complements the high-V2 5/1 observation 06ebbf6e52fa3ea6aef3 and tests whether the endpoint shift persists when the sample amount is reduced.

The 50/1 m177 condition is a deliberately strong extrapolation from the observed m177 points ce14dd2481560a984aea, aa43fe84c0d8c825fe58, and 34aaca6f7a0768d743fe; its large predicted V2 range can reveal whether the late-endpoint behavior continues at weaker eluent.
A matched 50/1 m177 loading contrast with 5b7151c95c4e964a121b tests whether any extreme V2 response is loading-sensitive rather than solely a nitrobenzophenone condition effect.

This 0/1 m141 point extends the basic heteroaromatic response below the observed 5/1 and 10/1 points 65f4f125b5e1f8137bd9 and 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0, testing whether the unusual retention trend is monotonic.
The 10/1 m141 point at intermediate loading targets the large basic-ring failure seen at 10/1 in 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 and helps locate the solvent-strength transition.

This matched 10/1 m141 point at higher loading forms a controlled contrast with abca62b372239d49a61b, testing conditional loading effects in the scaffold with the largest observed basic-ring residual.
A low-strength 0/1 m160 point at high loading extends the aminobenzonitrile curve beyond the observed 2/1 and 5/1 points 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90.
The same 0/1 m160 condition at lower loading pairs with f9a0fbbcf2f61d3843a5, testing whether the large 5/1 V2 shift is coupled to loading or mainly to mobile-phase composition.
This 2/1 low-loading m160 point bridges the measured 2/1 and 5/1 conditions and can discriminate a smooth basic-scaffold response from an abrupt high-strength transition.
The 0/1 m104 point supplies a weak-solvent anchor for the amino ester/basic environment, complementing the strongly underpredicted weaker-condition observation 6ce2b891280aed137ab8.
A 50/1 m104 point tests whether the amino ester endpoint remains late at strong PE-rich conditions and whether the model's V2 correction transfers across amino ester conditions.

This 5/1 m204 low-loading point probes the solvent region between the low-retention 1/1 observations a3560ac8164465dbb406 and c46b86dae7e6845f08cd and the very late 10/1 alcohol observation 73502a52708e4f9c2391.
Matched to 45ee5106187dc3b895e1 at higher loading, this experiment tests whether the striking m204 condition response is loading-dependent or primarily a free-alcohol solvent interaction.
The 2/1 m120 point lies between the observed 1/1 and 5/1 regimes, where 880646809d9f015053f6 and 71abc36775b6cce56da7 show very different retention; it can constrain the response curve.
A matched higher-loading 2/1 m120 point with 4ee22742c686bdbb1cb9 tests whether the large m120 contrast is a condition effect or a loading interaction.
This low-loading 2/1 m67 point complements the observed 10/1 and 20/1 secondary-alcohol responses 5e784130c58b8175024e and c627405cf70a0daacc94, providing a solvent-response anchor.
A second low-loading m67 point at 20/1 tests whether the late endpoint seen at 20/1 in c627405cf70a0daacc94 persists independently of the higher sample amount.
This 0/1 m199 loading point extends the sulfoxide curve below the observed 0/1 point b2bf97a1dcb9d6609f7d and tests whether the strong 5/1 outlier f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c is condition-specific.
The matched 2/1 m199 loading point complements 9ddc2e8babb52ee8e772 and tests whether the weaker-solvent sulfoxide response is stable across loading.
This 10/1 m146 point targets the quinoline-like failure represented by 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12 and probes whether high retention persists at a different condition.
The 1/1 m146 point provides a less extreme condition anchor for comparison with the large 5/1 m146 residual 04a2e8ad27ca641a3a12, helping separate topology from solvent response.
This weak-solvent m216 point samples the low end of a quinoline-like response curve, complementing the high-retention fused basic observation 1ae3618ec277b0463686.
The 10/1 m216 point tests whether the high basic-heteroaromatic retention seen in 1ae3618ec277b0463686 transfers across solvent strength and endpoint.
A lower-loading 50/1 m114 point forms a controlled contrast to the high-retention polyaromatic carbonyl observation 0cf0d36290765378ae8d and tests loading effects in an acceptor-rich scaffold.
This 20/1 m178 point maps the condition response below the large 50/1 V2 residual 0c5c35afb3a24375c153, testing whether the polycarbonyl error grows progressively with weaker solvent.
The 0/1 m178 point provides a low-retention anchor for the same polycarbonyl scaffold and helps distinguish a broad structural V2 bias from a condition-dependent one.
This lower-loading 50/1 m159 point is directly paired with the observed 50/1 high-retention example 1395836aef00d6a880b0, testing whether the cyano benzophenone endpoint is loading-sensitive.
A weak-solvent m159 point broadens the condition curve below the large 50/1 error in 1395836aef00d6a880b0 and tests transfer across polyacceptor chemistry.
This higher-loading 10/1 m13 point extends the observed multifunctional acceptor condition 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b and tests whether its V1/V2 underprediction persists with more sample.
The 0/1 m13 point supplies a weak-solvent anchor for the multifunctional ester/ketone scaffold and helps distinguish a structural bias from the observed high-condition residual 9e3f598e00375ec93d9b.
This 20/1 m209 alcohol/ether point bridges the observed high-retention 50/1 result 80f546c47198fa7c6dbf and weaker donor-containing conditions, testing transfer of alcohol-context corrections.

hypotheses.content: Mobile-phase ratio produces scaffold-specific, sometimes non-monotonic endpoint responses; V2 can change much more than V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The catalog contains many repeated scaffolds across PE/EA ratios, so learning local condition-response shapes can correct systematic V2 extrapolation errors across related rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which scaffold families show smooth solvent response and which show abrupt or non-monotonic V2 transitions?

hypotheses.content: Basic-ring topology, nitrogen accessibility, and amino-ester position create environment-specific retention responses that cannot be represented by a uniform nitrogen-count correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Basic and amino-containing rows include both severe underprediction and near-correct cases, making them useful for learning topology and condition interactions rather than applying a global nitrogen correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the new quinoline-like and amino-ester curves separate ring topology effects from mobile-phase-specific ion or silica interactions?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount affects endpoints strongly in some scaffolds but weakly in others; its effect must be modeled jointly with scaffold and mobile-phase condition.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled loading pairs can teach the model when its loading feature should shift V1/V2 and when condition or functional-group effects dominate.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the matched m125, m177, m141, m160, m204, m120, m199, m114, and m159 pairs show transferable loading slopes?

hypotheses.content: V2 underprediction is concentrated in multifunctional acceptor-rich, polycarbonyl, nitrocarbonyl, and cyano-aromatic scaffolds, especially at late-eluting conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These rows contribute large V2 loss and are represented across several chemical families, so endpoint-specific corrections may generalize beyond a single scaffold.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the V2 residual grow with acceptor multiplicity and aromatic carbonyl content after controlling for solvent ratio and loading?

hypotheses.content: Free-alcohol retention depends strongly on OH environment, neighboring ether/aromatic groups, and condition/loading context rather than on HBD count alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Alcohol-containing rows span the largest observed retention differences and can improve transfer of donor accessibility and solvent-response features across the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can matched alcohol curves distinguish OH accessibility from neighboring ether, aromatic, and loading effects?

hypotheses.content: Diphenyl sulfoxide has a condition-specific V2 anomaly: weaker-solvent points are near the local response while the strong-solvent point is substantially later than predicted.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched sulfoxide conditions can determine whether the large residual is a functional-group representation failure or a localized condition-response failure.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do loading-matched 0/1 and 2/1 sulfoxide points retain the observed endpoint trend without reproducing the 5/1 anomaly?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes strengthened the view that mobile-phase condition often dominates loading: m120, m160, m86, m141, and m204 showed large condition-dependent endpoint shifts, while the matched m204 1/1 loading pair had nearly identical V2 values. The earlier loading hypothesis therefore remains conditional rather than universal; the m120 5/1 pair still demonstrates a large scaffold-specific loading effect, while m181 and m204 provide useful weak-loading counterexamples. Large V2 errors persisted for m125, m13, m159, m178, and the high-condition polycarbonyl and basic-ring families, motivating more local endpoint curves. The previous chalcone/dibenzalacetone onset-transfer hypothesis and the mesityl steric-shielding hypothesis remain rejected by their measured onset values. The sulfoxide results now look condition-specific because its weaker-solvent points are much closer to the observed trend than the strong-solvent outlier.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates on scientifically connected local experiments rather than a single predicted volume. It contains matched loading pairs for m177, m141, m160, m204, m120, m199, m114, and m159; condition-response points for m125, m67, m146, m216, m178, m13, and m209; and basic, alcohol, sulfoxide, and acceptor-rich families with distinct silica-interaction environments. Several choices repair regions with repeated V2 underprediction, while the low-strength anchors and matched pairs test whether those corrections generalize or are scaffold-specific. This combination should improve the model's structure-condition-loading interactions and reduce endpoint-specific residuals across the broader Row-distribution.
